title: BTS Closes US Continental ARIRANG Tour Leg with El Paso Night 2 — Las Vegas (May 23–28) Is Next
detail: On May 3, 2026 — Day 4,707 since BTS's June 13, 2013 debut — BTS performs the second and final night at Sun Bowl Stadium in El Paso, Texas, closing out the US continental portion of the ARIRANG World Tour. Both El Paso shows sold out, drawing an estimated 100,000+ fans across the two nights from across West Texas, New Mexico, Arizona, and northern Mexico, with significant cross-border attendance from Ciudad Juárez. The El Paso run marks BTS's first-ever performances in the border region, described by local media as a landmark cultural and economic event for the city. With the El Paso leg complete, the ARIRANG World Tour's next North American dates are at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas: May 23, 24, 27, and 28 — four nights at the 65,000-capacity venue. The Asian leg follows in June, with sold-out shows at Busan Asiad Main Stadium on June 12–13 (the group's 13th debut anniversary). The ARIRANG World Tour spans 85+ dates, 34 cities, and 23 countries. UTEP Office of Special Events confirmed both nights ran to schedule with no major incidents, a marked contrast to the Night 1 audio malfunction during the Tampa leg (April 25). Surprise songs for Night 2 were not confirmed in official sources at time of publication.

title: 'SWIM' Moves to ~No. 22 on Billboard Hot 100 in Week 5 — Five Consecutive Weeks Charting
detail: In its fifth week on the Billboard Hot 100 (chart dated ~May 3, 2026), BTS's 'SWIM' falls from No. 10 to approximately No. 22, completing five consecutive weeks on the chart since its debut at No. 1 on the March 27 chart. The single tracks: No. 1 (debut, week 1) → No. 2 (week 2) → No. 5 (week 3) → No. 10 (week 4) → ~No. 22 (week 5). The drop-off pattern is consistent with BTS's prior singles in the streaming era, where physical sales peak drive chart position before radio airplay and streaming carry sustain. 'Body to Body' continues to chart on the Hot 100 alongside 'SWIM,' while 'ARIRANG' remains in the top 5 of the Billboard 200 in its seventh week. The ongoing ARIRANG World Tour continues to drive merchandise and album equivalent units that support sustained chart performance. 'SWIM' topped the Billboard Global 200 for four consecutive weeks — the longest run at No. 1 on that chart by a K-pop act — and set a Pop Radio Airplay record for a Korean act (peak No. 13). Combined, 'SWIM' has accumulated over 500 million global streams in its first five weeks, according to Spotify tracking data.

media.caption: 'SWIM' completes five consecutive weeks on the Billboard Hot 100, peaking at No. 1 before settling at ~No. 22 in week 5
